newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close up in hefty trade on options.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close up in hefty trade on options.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended higher in huge but calm trade amid options settlements, despite a sharp drop in Cia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) on fears its April 29 privatization auction may be suspended, brokers said.
"Vale fell because of concerns about an injunction," one local trader told Reuters.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa .BVSP index of 49 most- traded shares closed up 0.55 percent at 9,474 points on enormous trade of 2.93 billion reais ($2.77 billion) as options came due.
Experts said Tuesday's volume was close to a daily record for the Sao Paulo bolsa, which normally trades $400 million to $500 million, except on options expiry when volume surges.
Much of the trade was in bellwether Telebras, which normally accounts for 60 percent of daily stock volume and 90 percent of options trade.

Telebras' preferred shares rose 0.26 percent to end at 117.00 reais, in volatile trade between holders of options with strike prices of 115 reais and 120 reais. Electrical shares also posted gains, prompting a 1.01 percent rise in the Electrical sector Index .IEE to close at 2,642 points.
The jump was led by blue-chip Eletrobras, which soared 1.86 percent to end the day at 484.00 reais.
Depsite the bolsa's overall rise, CVRD dropped on fears that lawsuits would likely spark a delay in the planned April 29 auction of a maximum 45 percent controlling satake in the company.
Late in the day, a Supreme Court judge granted an injunction that threatened to derail the auction, but government officials insisted the sale date would not be changed.
CVRD's preferred blue chip closed down 1.34 percent at 25.75 reais, but had been down even more during the afternoon.
Among the top risers was state oil firm Petrobras's preferred share, which ended up 2.43 percent to close at 210.50 reais.
